function.mechanism: Scavenges radicals and slows oxidative deterioration of fats/oils, reducing rancidity in food matrices.

adi.basis: EFSA re-evaluation maintained the ADI set by SCF and reported no genotoxicity concern; exposure statement later discussed potential exceedance in conservative combined scenarios.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA re-evaluation did not identify genotoxicity concern; refined exposure work indicated possible ADI exceedance in some high-consumer child groups under combined-assumption scenarios.

adi.basis: JECFA ADI is expressed as 0-0.5 mg/kg bw (upper bound 0.5), with evaluation year 1988 in WHO/JECFA chemical entry.

concerns.summary: IARC classification lists BHA as Group 2B; JECFA toxicological monograph discusses high-dose forestomach lesions/tumors in rats with uncertain direct human relevance.
Recent zebrafish embryo-larval study reports developmental and neurobehavioral disruption after low-ppb BHA exposure.
Recent hESC-derived hepatocyte model study on 3-BHA (BHA isomer) reported developmental hepatotoxicity-associated signals.
Mouse co-exposure study (nanoplastics plus 3-BHA) reported aggravated kidney injury via TGF-beta/SMAD pathway, indicating potential concern in mixed-exposure contexts.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA re-evaluation reported no concern with respect to genotoxicity.
Ex vivo human gut microbiome study found minimal effect under tested BHA conditions.

populations: high consumers under conservative combined-exposure assumptions
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA refined exposure statement and WHO/JECFA intake text indicate potential exceedance in upper-end consumer scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: BHA remains regulated/authorized with explicit limits, but credible caveats remain: IARC Group 2B classification, high-dose animal hazard findings, and modeled exceedance risk in some child/high-consumer scenarios.
key_factors: EFSA ADI of 1.0 mg/kg bw/day with no genotoxicity concern
JECFA ADI 0-0.5 mg/kg bw and intake exceedance caveat for high consumers
CFR conditions and concentration limits in 21 CFR 172.110 and 182.3169
Recent experimental studies indicating potential neurodevelopmental/hepatic/renal concerns
